To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) spouses provide each other with attachment security, (b) this security has important implications for marital functioning, (c) this security does not depend on marital satisfaction, (d) this security is not dependent on how the spouse feels about the marriage, (e) this security has implications for the spouses’ functioning outside the marriage (e.g., with respect to their exploration), and (f) attachment style has implications for marital functioning

(a) attachment security in marriage is a distinct construct, independent of marital satisfaction; (b) the two constructs are correlated; and (c) attachment security is associated with more positive outcomes than satisfaction, including more effective emotion regulation, less physiological arousal in response to stress, and better mental health and well-being

(a) marital satisfaction is a poor predictor of the extent to which a spouse provides the attachment figure’s functions, (b) the extent to which spouses provide the attachment figure’s function is a good predictor of marital satisfaction, and (c) attachment style is a good predictor, both of the extent to the extent which a spouse provides attachment figure’s functions and of the extent to how satisfied a spouse is with the relationship.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attachment in marital functioning.
the nature of the relationship between marital satisfaction and marital functioning, and the role of attachment in marital functioning.
understanding marital relationships in terms of their contribution to the security of each spouse’s attachment system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attachment theory has a great deal to offer the study of marital functioning and satisfaction.

marital satisfaction, as a global evaluation of the relationship, is a poor predictor of relationship quality, whereas a more specific assessment of the quality of interactional processes is a much better predictor.
the quality of attachment in marriage, and not the quality of the marriage itself, is the key to a satisfying relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quality of a marital relationship is not simply a matter of how well the couple is able to meet one another’s needs for satisfaction, security, and self-actualization, but also of the quality of the attachment bond that exists between them.
marital relationships are more than a source of satisfaction and fulfillment.
attachment theory provides a framework for conceptualizing and understanding how spouses provide each other with the resources necessary to maintain a secure base and explore the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the attachment bond, as a source of security and support, is an important component of marital functioning, independent of marital satisfaction.
attachment theory can be used to explain how spouses provide a sense of felt security to each other.
attachment is an important factor in marital relationships and that attachment theory can provide a framework to better understand the role of attachment in marriage.
